## Description
**What**: Publish plugins/dso/docs/contracts/mutation-testing-findings.md (per-stack-result schema, aggregate-result schema with schema_version=1, unknown-field passthrough) and ship plugins/dso/workflows/mutation-testing.yml as a plugin template running a Python (mutmut) matrix job in calibration mode.
**Why**: This is the walking skeleton — the minimum end-to-end path proving the mutation-testing concept (contract -> CI run -> findings JSON -> PR comment) before polyglot expansion.
**Scope**:
- IN: findings contract markdown; mutation-testing.yml with pull_request trigger (types synchronize, opened; no branches filter; no pull_request_target; no push, per Operational Constraints Probe-2); concurrency group keyed to github.head_ref; skip-mutation-testing label opt-out; mutation.max_files_per_run (default 100) auto-skip with annotation; mutmut pinned to mutation.python.tool_version with mutation.python.fallback_versions chain and TOOL_INSTALL_FAILED annotation; incremental run over diffed Python files; findings JSON per contract; actions/upload-artifact telemetry; aggregate job upserting a PR comment with MUTATION_TESTING_FINDINGS_<pr-number> marker; GHA-summary-only fallback for fork PRs; scope-seal header block (SC8 in-workflow portion); dso-config.conf mutation.* default keys for Python; CLAUDE.md/contracts-index references are OUT (draft-8).
- OUT: Ruby/JS-TS/Go stacks; calibration auto-surfacing; threshold enforcement; onboarding/setup-script integration; standalone doc addenda.

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, plugins/dso/docs/contracts/mutation-testing-findings.md exists and documents the per-stack-result schema, the aggregate-result schema with schema_version=1, and the unknown-field passthrough requirement ← Satisfies: sc-1
- When this story is complete, tooling that parses a findings JSON containing an unrecognized field re-emits that field unchanged in its output ← Satisfies: sc-1
- When this story is complete, plugins/dso/workflows/mutation-testing.yml triggers on pull_request types synchronize and opened with no branches filter, declares a concurrency group keyed to github.head_ref, contains no pull_request_target block, and contains no push block ← Satisfies: sc-2
- When this story is complete, a PR carrying the skip-mutation-testing label runs the workflow without executing the mutmut job and a PR whose mutable-file count exceeds mutation.max_files_per_run auto-skips with an annotation ← Satisfies: sc-2
- When this story is complete, the Python job installs mutmut at mutation.python.tool_version, falls back through mutation.python.fallback_versions on install failure, emits TOOL_INSTALL_FAILED on final failure, runs incremental mutation over diffed Python files, writes findings JSON per the contract, uploads it as a workflow artifact, and the aggregate job upserts a PR comment marked MUTATION_TESTING_FINDINGS_<pr-number> with a GHA-summary-only fallback ← Satisfies: sc-2
- When this story is complete, the mutation-testing.yml header contains the verbatim SCOPE-SEALED bash-out-of-scope block referencing the 411b epic and listing the supported stacks ← Satisfies: sc-8
- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic (findings-JSON emission, passthrough preservation, max_files_per_run skip-check, fallback-version chain) ← Satisfies: sc-2

## Considerations

- [Reliability] The aggregate PR-comment marker MUTATION_TESTING_FINDINGS_<pr-number> must be distinct from llm-review's marker so no comment-write race is possible.
- [Cost] Concurrency cancellation on new commits and the max_files_per_run pre-flight are the primary per-PR cost controls.
- [Observability] Per EXTERNAL FRAMING (silent-sensor caution): mutants_generated is a distinct field; zero indicates the PR touched only non-mutable code and must not be conflated with a perfect kill rate.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a DSO maintainer, I want a published findings contract and a Python-pilot mutation-testing CI workflow, so that PRs touching Python code report calibration-mode kill-rate telemetry.
